Customer to share 72h sample workload traces and p95 SLA targets by 2025-08-11
Schedule throughput/latency benchmark on Dedicated cluster for week of 2025-08-19 (Redwood/Marcus to confirm exact slot)

Tom Hayes: Prepare benchmark plan + list of required sample prompts/traces (due 2025-08-11)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-08-07 09:30 PT / 16:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes (recording includes pre/post chat)
Attendees: Emma Liu (Redwood AE), Tom Hayes (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Kronos Head of ML), Marcus Klein (Kronos Infra Lead), Priya Desai (Kronos Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Quick scoping to align on what success looks like for the POC, how many tokens/requests we expect, benchmarking plan, and what commercial credits/terms Redwood can offer while Kronos evaluates procurement path.

[00:00] Emma Liu: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Emma from Redwood. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sarah Patel: Good thanks, Emma. Busy week but excited to get this scoped, we've been trying to size this pilot so we can get internal buy-in.
[00:22] Tom Hayes: Hi folks, Tom here, SE. I'll drive the tech scoping and benchmark plan. Apologies if I talk too deep, I'll try to keep to the agenda.
[00:34] Marcus Klein: Marcus - infra. We'll be the ones doing validation on our side and running the sample requests against Redwood Dedicated if needed.
[00:40] Priya Desai: Priya from procurement - I'll need the commercial guardrails and an approximate timeline for approvals.

[01:05] Emma Liu: Quick run-through: goal is to agree on success criteria, get a workload trace from Kronos, land a pilot credit allocation and SOW, and then schedule a benchmark run. We're thinking a 6-week pilot with a limited credit pool but flexible conversions to reserved capacity if it goes well. Thoughts?
[01:26] Sarah Patel: That lines up. For success, we need p95 under 400ms for single-turn prompts and throughput of about 150 requests/sec for the rerank pipeline. Also quality — less than 3% hallucination / incorrect re-ranks on our eval set.
[01:47] Tom Hayes: Helpful — can you confirm average sequence length and tokens per request? That drives cost and which model/quantization we recommend.
[01:57] Sarah Patel: Avg 128 tokens, typically between 64-256. Rerank batch size to be about 32 per call.
[02:09] Marcus Klein: Also worth noting our current infra uses 40GB A100s on-prem and some GCP VMs for staging. We'll want to compare Redwood Dedicated against our internal baseline.
[02:22] Emma Liu: Understood. For the commercial side, we usually propose credit allocations for pilots — given your expected load and that avg token figure, initial suggestion is 50k token-equivalent credits + discounted overage. That roughly maps to the benchmark runs and initial production-esque testing.
[02:44] Priya Desai: Can you put that 50k into dollar terms or a slab? Procurement needs a notional $ figure to fast-track.
[02:51] Emma Liu: Absolutely — we'll include both tokens and dollar estimate in the SOW. Tom, any rough econ for 128 avg seq at p95 400ms?
[03:03] Tom Hayes: Rough back of envelope: if you're using a mid-size open model on Dedicated with batching and kv-cache, unit cost after batching could be lower — pilot credits of 50k tokens should support a few days of stress testing plus eval runs. I'll prepare a more detailed cost table.
[03:20] Sarah Patel: Also, for the accuracy metric, we have a 2k example eval set we'll share. We need Redwood to run the eval and flag regression vs baseline.
[03:32] Tom Hayes: Good — we'll add that to the benchmark plan. We usually rerun baseline against your eval set and provide precision/recall-ish metrics and a hallucination/performance delta.
[03:45] Marcus Klein: Operationally, how long does it take to spin a Dedicated test pool? If we need to test on a specific GPU type (e.g., A100-40GB), what's the lead time?
[03:58] Emma Liu: For dedicated pilot capacity, we can provision in 3-5 business days for standard pool templates. If it's a very specific shape we may need a week. For faster start we'll route you to a compatible variant and note the exact GPU in the plan.
[04:12] Sarah Patel: OK, timeline matters — procurement window is ~3 weeks for small pilots, longer for anything with legal entanglements.
[04:20] Priya Desai: Correct. We need quote, SOW, security docs (SOC2) and a simple MSA or pilot addendum. Can Redwood provide standard SOC2 and data processing addenda?
[04:34] Emma Liu: Yes; we have SOC 2 and DPAs. We'll attach security pack and a light MSA/pilot addendum template.
[04:42] Tom Hayes: Quick technical note — if you opt for VPC/private, that alters timeline and we should factor firewall/peering steps. For the benchmark we can run in Redwood Dedicated in our cloud region first.
[05:00] Marcus Klein: That works. For comparability, we need logs: p95, tail latency, token counts per request, and GPU utilization.
[05:10] Tom Hayes: We'll capture those metrics and produce a side-by-side. We're also going to capture KV cache hit rates — sorry that sometimes shows up as KV "cash" in our older tools, but we mean cache — and batching efficiency.
[05:25] Sarah Patel: (laughs) I saw KV cash in older notes too.

[06:10] Emma Liu: Let's pin success criteria now: 1) p95 latency < 400ms single-turn, 2) Throughput: 150 req/s sustained for reranker, 3) Quality: <=3% hallucination on your eval set, 4) Cost: < $X per 1M tokens in pilot projection (we'll define $X in SOW). Everyone OK with those?
[06:31] Sarah Patel: Yes, those look fine. We might also add 99th percentile SLO as a check.
[06:39] Marcus Klein: Add GPU utilization and stability — no OOMs under the target load.
[06:45] Tom Hayes: We'll include 99p and stability checks.

[08:00] Emma Liu: On commercial guardrails: for pilots we do credits + a lightweight SOW. Typically 6 weeks is the sweet spot: 2 weeks for integration, 2 weeks for benchmark testing, 2 weeks for evaluation and handoff / decisions. If we need to compress, we can, but costs and the scope of what we cover change.
[08:20] Priya Desai: 6 weeks fits internal procurement faster lane. For contracting, minimal redlines: we'd ask for a pilot addendum to limit term and liability. We won't sign a full-term MSA until procurement finalizes.
[08:36] Emma Liu: Understood. We'll provide a pilot addendum template this week that includes credit burn rules, a termination clause, and conversion mechanics (how credits become reserved capacity or billed usage).
[08:50] Sarah Patel: One more: data retention. We need clarity that any logs from the eval won't be used to train Redwood models and that keys are handled securely.
[09:02] Tom Hayes: We have a data policy section in the security pack and KMS options for keys. We'll call out non-training guarantee in the DPA.

[10:15] Emma Liu: Benchmark plan — Tom, do you want to outline?
[10:18] Tom Hayes: Sure. Step 1: collect 72-hour trace and eval set (customer). Step 2: Redwood runs a baseline test on Dedicated with compatible model config (we'll propose model variants: fp16, int8-quant). Step 3: run throughput sweep — 50/100/150/200 reqs/sec — measure p50/p95/99 and GPU util. Step 4: run quality eval on your 2k set and produce hallucination/regression matrix. Step 5: deliver report and recommended production profile.
[10:45] Sarah Patel: Sounds good. How long will the Redwood run take once traces are in?
[10:50] Tom Hayes: Once we have traces, 2-3 business days for a full sweep and report, assuming we have pilot credits and the dedicated pool lined up.
[10:57] Marcus Klein: If we provide a trimmed subset first can we get quicker feedback?
[11:03] Tom Hayes: Yes, a 12-hour sample will get you preliminary numbers in 24 hours. We'll still do full sweep later.

[12:20] Priya Desai: About the credits — can you put guardrails on usage? We want to avoid unexpected overages during testing.
[12:28] Emma Liu: We'll set hard caps on the pilot credit pool and optionally notify at 75%/90% burn. Overage needs pre-approval and won't auto-charge without PO.
[12:40] Priya Desai: Good. Also, what is the conversion path if the pilot is successful? Do we move to reserved Dedicated capacity with a commit?
[12:49] Emma Liu: Yes — pilot can convert to reserved capacity or continue as pay-as-you-go. We'll include an option in the SOW that shows pricing for a 3/6/12 month committed pool and the steps to convert credits to committed credit.
[13:05] Sarah Patel: From a stakeholder perspective, what do we need to show execs? A simple one-page ROI with expected latency gains and cost delta.
[13:14] Emma Liu: We'll prepare a one-pager ROI and include sample numbers from the benchmark.

[15:00] Tom Hayes: Quick clarifying note: when you run rerank pipelines, are you doing single requests with batch sizes or multi-call orchestration? It changes batching patterns.
[15:12] Sarah Patel: Our current flow is microservice that batches 32 per call for the reranker, so we expect bigger batch efficiency but need per-call latency under 400ms.
[15:25] Tom Hayes: OK we'll set the benchmark to replicate that exact batch size.

[17:45] Marcus Klein: On security docs — I need a contact for more detailed SOC/ISO questions.
[17:50] Emma Liu: I'll cc our security lead, Priya (internal) — sorry same first name — but I'll include the security pack and contact.
[18:00] Priya Desai (customer): Please do, we will need the SOC2 Type II and DPA.

[20:10] Emma Liu: Anything else on the SOW level? Pricing bands, conversion mechanics, termination?
[20:18] Priya Desai: If you include a clear termination and liability cap for the pilot we're comfortable. Also include the conversion discounts up front so procurement can compare.
[20:30] Emma Liu: We'll add conversion discounts for 3/6/12m reserved terms.

[25:00] Replay of earlier point / some cross talk and a short pause as folks look through notes.

[30:00] Tom Hayes: One more technical ask — please provide your current error rate and what percentage of requests are long-tail >256 tokens. That helps recommend quantization vs fp16.
[30:12] Marcus Klein: We actually have telemetry showing 12% over 256 tokens for edge cases, but 75% are under 128. We'll attach telemetry slice.
[30:22] Sarah Patel: We'll sanitize traces before sending.

[36:00] Emma Liu: Let's confirm timeline: Redwood sends draft SOW/credit proposal + security pack by 2025-08-09. Kronos provides traces and procurement timeline by 2025-08-11. Benchmark scheduled week of 2025-08-19. Is that feasible?
[36:18] Marcus Klein: Yes.
[36:22] Priya Desai: Works for procurement's fast lane.
[36:26] Sarah Patel: Yes, will prioritize.

[40:00] Tom Hayes: Small note re: observability — we'll include per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown in the report so you can show cost per rerank.
[40:09] Sarah Patel: Perfect.

[45:30] Emma Liu: Recap / next steps: 1) Emma will send pilot credit terms and SOW (due 2025-08-09). 2) Tom will send benchmark plan and sample prompt list (due 2025-08-11). 3) Marcus will provide traces + topology (due 2025-08-11). 4) Priya will share procurement approver list and timeline (due 2025-08-14). 5) Schedule bench week of 8/19.

[46:05] Sarah Patel: Thanks, appreciate the alignment. One small ask — can Redwood include an initial smoke test in the SOW so we can validate connectivity quickly?
[46:16] Emma Liu: Yes we'll include a 1-day smoke test in week 1.

[48:00] End of core call — folks do some off-agenda clarifications for another ~14 minutes then hang up.

Auto-generated action items appended above.

References/shared artifacts mentioned: "security pack (SOC2/DPA)" (will be attached in follow up), "pilot SOW/credits spreadsheet", "2k eval set + 72h traces".

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlap present, some transcription errors like "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", occasional missing punctuation.

Call ended with explicit next steps and agreement to proceed with pilot SOW and benchmark scheduling.
